claim: A random true-label risk survey outperforms a frozen unlabeled proxy when all outcome labels shift.
PPS augmented risk estimation outperforms uniform random surveys when the confident part of label mechanism changes.
PPS augmented risk estimation improves over random surveys when the uncertain part of labeling changes.
Proportionally stratifying model uncertainty improves over SRS under high-confidence label drift.
Neyman proxy-based allocation improves over proportional allocation when rare systematic error flips occur.
